newsitem.title: USA: Yale raises tender offer for notes.
newsitem.headline: Yale raises tender offer for notes.

text.p: Columbus McKinnon Corp said on Friday that its majority-owned Yale Industries Inc is increasing its tender offer for all $70 million of the company's 11-1/2 percent senior secured notes due 2000.
The company is offering to pay 108.250 percent of the outstanding principal amount of the notes, an increase from 108.125 percent of the principal amount, Columbus McKinnon said.

Yale amended the tender offer to increase the aggregate consideration to be paid in the tender offer to 108.250 percent of principal, consisting of an offer to purchase the notes for 106.750 percent of principal and a consent solicitation payment of 1.500 percent of principal amount of notes, the company said.
Completion is condutioned upon receipt of a majority in principal of the outstanding notes, the company said.
Yale's tender offer is set to expire 1700 EST on Friday December 13, 1996, Columbus McKinnon said.
Bear Stearns & Co Inc is the dealer manager for the tender offer, Columbus McKinnon said.
